architecture.fell_back_and_why: Budget cap of three concurrent sub-agents meant one wave, not two. Wave 1 covered the three partitions the supervisor had not read (PHP, Java/Vert.x, MLflow gateway); the supervisor read edge-fleet-salt, ledger-etl-airflow and courier_app in full itself and acted as researcher for them, so the planned wave 2 was dropped rather than run. Consequence, stated plainly: those three partitions had one pair of eyes instead of two, and their findings were not independently second-opinioned the way the wave-1 partitions were reviewed by the supervisor against source. Conversely, support-desk-api effectively got two independent researchers -- the sub-agent and the supervisor, who had read it while waiting -- and they converged on the same eight findings with the same eight CWEs; the two severity disagreements (mass assignment, legacy search) were adjudicated at the critic stage and the more conservative call was taken in both. Stages 2-4 (architecture, threat model, plan) were folded into the supervisor context and written to mantis-work/workspace/kb/THREAT_MODEL.md rather than delegated, because the whole target is 3,590 lines and delegating a KB build over it would have cost more than it returned. The mantis workspace state machine (.mantis_state.json, per-finding UUID JSONs, archive/, snapshot pinning) was not materialised: this is a single-pass run with no --sync, so MODE-OFF applies, active_snapshot is absent by contract, and findings were assembled directly into the requested report file.
architecture.review_constraints_mapping: FP-nn labels are the mantis-review skill's own thirteen negative constraints, in its order: FP-01 ignore_hypothetical_misuse, FP-02 ignore_missing_hygiene, FP-03 require_strict_reproducibility, FP-04 avoid_pedantic_linting, FP-05 no_security_flaw_stretching, FP-06 evaluate_questionable_file_paths, FP-07 ignore_resource_exhaustion_dos, FP-08 intrinsic_security_flaws, FP-09 verify_mitigations_pragmatically, FP-10 refine_code_paths_strictly, FP-11 ignore_simd_vector_padding, FP-12 ensure_source_code_coherence, FP-13 verify_attacker_control_of_source. 'HOLDS' means the constraint fires against the finding; 'DOES_NOT_HOLD' means it does not. FP-10 and FP-11 are omitted from every triage list: FP-10 is a housekeeping rule about trimming code_paths rather than a validity test, and FP-11 concerns SIMD padding contracts, which no language in this corpus has.

stages_skipped: mantis-history -- the target is not a VCS repository (git rev-parse fails, no .git/.hg/.repo anywhere under TARGET), so there is no history to mine and workspace/historical_learnings.jsonl would be empty by construction.

mantis-structural-index -- the snapshot ships no workspace/helpers/query_structural_index.py and no prebuilt SCIP/Kythe index; the skill is explicitly HINT-only and degrades to grep, which is what was used. Skipping it changes no verdict.

mantis-reproduce -- offline and read-only. No PHP, JVM, Airflow, Salt master, Flutter toolchain or MLflow runtime is available, and building a sandboxed service for each of six stacks was outside the budget. No finding is marked reproduced; every status is confirmed-by-reading or probable.
mantis-patch -- the brief forbids modifying anything under TARGET, and mantis-patch writes fixes into the code root. Recommendations are given per finding instead, and no re-attack loop was run.

mantis-reflect -- the harness exposes sub-agent transcripts only as JSONL files the supervisor is instructed not to read, so per-stage trajectories could not be parsed. Per the skill's own fallback this is recorded as a missing-transcript skip rather than a silent zero-learnings pass.
mantis-researcher wave 2 -- planned as an independent second opinion on edge-fleet-salt, ledger-etl-airflow and courier_app; dropped under the budget cap after wave 1 returned. See fell_back_and_why.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection in delivery_detail via string interpolation of the delivery id into rawQuery
ruled_out.killed_by: deliveryId is declared final int (delivery_detail.dart:19) and the only construction sites pass int.tryParse output (main.dart:42, which returns on null) or the same typed field (delivery_detail.dart:56). Dart's type system makes the interpolation non-injectable; the mitigation pragmatically works.

ruled_out.assertion: Command injection in AdminController::logs, where the journal unit is concatenated into shell_exec
ruled_out.killed_by: Neither operand is request-controlled: $unit comes from getenv('LOG_UNIT') with a literal fallback (settings.php:38) and $lines is int-cast twice, at :83 and again at :86. No attacker ingress reaches the sink. The real defect on this endpoint is that it is unauthenticated, reported separately as CWE-306.

ruled_out.assertion: Column-name SQL injection through the generic Db::update writer
ruled_out.killed_by: The column is wrapped in backticks with every backtick stripped from the value, so injected text cannot leave the quoted identifier and MySQL rejects it as an unknown column. The abuse that does work through this path -- writing unintended columns -- is reported as CWE-915.

ruled_out.assertion: ORDER BY / LIMIT injection in TicketController::index
ruled_out.killed_by: $sort passes a strict in_array allowlist (Sanitize.php:28), $dir collapses to the literal ASC or DESC (Sanitize.php:33), and $limit is int-cast and clamped to 1..200 (TicketController.php:31). Only the status fragment on the line above is injectable.

ruled_out.assertion: Unrestricted file upload leading to code execution via POST /tickets/{id}/attachments
ruled_out.killed_by: Sanitize::filename is applied at :41 and holds at this call site: basename strips directory parts, the character class reduces everything outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] to underscore, and leading dots are trimmed. The storage root (settings.php:17) is outside public/, so an uploaded .php is never served.

ruled_out.assertion: Hardcoded database credentials in the PHP settings file
ruled_out.killed_by: Checked because FP-08 keeps hardcoded secrets in scope regardless of reachability -- but these are getenv() fallbacks for local development and the password fallback is the empty string. No secret material is committed.

ruled_out.assertion: Stack traces disclosed to clients by the PHP error middleware
ruled_out.killed_by: display_errors is driven by APP_DEBUG through FILTER_VALIDATE_BOOLEAN and defaults to false, so the shipped configuration does not leak traces. Enabling it is an operator decision.

ruled_out.assertion: pickle.load of a scratch cache file is an unsafe deserialization sink
ruled_out.killed_by: A repo-wide grep for read_cache and write_cache returns only the two definitions -- neither has a caller. Reporting it would require assuming a hypothetical future caller AND an attacker who can plant a file in the scratch directory. The tar-slip write primitive that could plant such a file is reported on its own terms as CWE-22.

ruled_out.assertion: dest_prefix reaches os.path.join in LedgerExportOperator without validation, giving path traversal into /mnt/finance-share
ruled_out.killed_by: The operator reads conf['dest_prefix'] directly rather than the validated xcom, but validate_conf (reconcile.py:34-38) gates the whole DAG and rejects any prefix that is empty, over 64 characters, or not alphanumeric after removing dashes and underscores -- '..' fails isalnum(). The mitigation works; reading the raw conf instead of the xcom is a defense-in-depth note, not a finding.

ruled_out.assertion: Command injection in archive_report, which builds a tar command and runs it with shell=True
ruled_out.killed_by: Every element is passed through shlex.quote before the join, and the only caller-influenced element (dest_prefix) is additionally alphanumeric-validated upstream. The mitigation pragmatically works.

ruled_out.assertion: Command injection in the per-region rollup BashOperator commands
ruled_out.killed_by: The templated values are params.region and params.work_root, sourced from settings.REGIONS (a fixed tuple, settings.py:7) and an env var read at import time. No request or trigger payload reaches them.

ruled_out.assertion: Hardcoded sandbox basic-auth credentials demo:demo in the ledger settings
ruled_out.killed_by: Documented at :25-26 as the vendor's published getting-started pair for a nightly-wiped shared sandbox tenant holding generated rows, and sandbox_probe (hooks.py:62) has no caller in the tree. No production credential is exposed.

ruled_out.assertion: Hardcoded vendor sandbox token in the Salt pillar
ruled_out.killed_by: Same shape: documented at :12-13 as published in the vendor's public quickstart and reaching only sandbox.fleetvendor.example, and fleetctl.sandbox_check (fleetctl.py:93) has no caller. Nothing production-bearing is disclosed.

ruled_out.assertion: Wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin on the nginx /assets/ location
ruled_out.killed_by: The location serves a static widget bundle with no cookies and no session (comment at :24) and does not set Allow-Credentials, so a wildcard is the correct configuration for a CDN-cached asset path. The credentialed CORS header three locations down is on /api/ and uses a concrete origin.

ruled_out.assertion: Publishable map-tiles key hardcoded in the Flutter client
ruled_out.killed_by: Documented at :23-24 as scoped to the tile endpoints and embedded in the vendor's own web demo -- a publishable token by design. Any key shipped in a mobile binary is extractable, so scoping is the control, and it is in place.

ruled_out.assertion: MainActivity is exported with BROWSABLE intent filters, allowing any app to launch it
ruled_out.killed_by: Export is required for the deep links the dispatch system sends by SMS to work at all. The defect is not that the activity is reachable but that the link parameters are unvalidated once inside, which is reported as CWE-200 and CWE-749.

ruled_out.assertion: Path traversal in the archive-vault preset download via the :name path parameter
ruled_out.killed_by: readPreset uses name only as a key into an immutable three-entry map (BlobStore.java:20-23) and returns a failed future on a miss (:66). The attacker string never reaches presetRoot.resolve -- only the mapped constant filename does.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection via the sort column in MetadataRepository.listByOwner, which String.formats it into ORDER BY
ruled_out.killed_by: sort.column() can only return one of three hardcoded identifiers, and SortColumn.parse falls back to CREATED_AT for any unmatched or null input. The allowlist works; claiming a bypass would be inventing one.

ruled_out.assertion: alg:none or algorithm-confusion bypass in the primary archive-vault token verification path
ruled_out.killed_by: jjwt 0.12.5 with verifyWith((SecretKey) signingKey) and parseSignedClaims pins verification to the HMAC key type and rejects unsecured JWTs; requireIssuer and requireAudience are both applied. Correct library use. Expiry is likewise enforced by parseSignedClaims and was checked separately.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection in RetentionSweeper.sweep, where bucket and keepDays are concatenated into the statement
ruled_out.killed_by: Both values come from the retention config object fed from config.json:18-22; keepDays is read with getInteger so it cannot carry SQL, and no HTTP handler writes the config. No attacker-controlled ingress.

ruled_out.assertion: Log forging and arbitrary blob deletion through an attacker-chosen document title and blob_key in the retention sweep
ruled_out.killed_by: Traced the write path rather than assuming it: title and blob_key are only ever written by MetadataRepository.insert, which a grep shows has zero call sites -- ingestManifest parses and echoes without persisting. With no reachable route that stores an attacker-chosen value, neither is concretely triggerable in this tree.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection in RunbookIndex.search, which builds its statement with an f-string
ruled_out.killed_by: The f-string interpolates only self.schema (from config, not the request) and int(k); collection and query travel as bound parameters, and k = int(k or self.top_k) raises on non-numeric input before reaching the string. Standard safe psycopg use.

ruled_out.assertion: probe_status is an SSRF sink equivalent to http_fetch
ruled_out.killed_by: guardrails.allowed_host is called first (tools.py:69) and matches urlparse(url).hostname against an exact-match set, which defeats userinfo and fragment tricks; follow_redirects is not enabled on this client. It is also filtered out of the dispatch registry because config.yaml does not list it. The mitigation works -- the finding is on its unguarded twin.

ruled_out.assertion: guardrails.redact fails to mask secrets before prompts are written to the audit log
ruled_out.killed_by: Best-effort redaction whose pattern list is incomplete by nature, and the gateway keys never appear in the rendered prompt or completion -- they arrive in a header and are not copied in. Enumerating missed patterns is defense-in-depth commentary.

ruled_out.assertion: max_tokens, top_k and repeated distinct model URIs let a caller drive unbounded cost, memory and cache churn
ruled_out.killed_by: Pure resource-exhaustion DoS, which the review constraints exclude. The security-relevant half of the cache-churn variant is already captured by the unvalidated model_uri finding.

ruled_out.assertion: BridgeKeyMiddleware compares client keys in a loop, leaking which key matched through response timing
ruled_out.killed_by: Each individual comparison uses hmac.compare_digest, the correct primitive; the residual signal across a two-entry dict is not a practical oracle for the key material, and claiming one would stretch a working mitigation.

ruled_out.assertion: Unhandled NumberFormatException on the archive-vault limit parameter
ruled_out.killed_by: ?limit=abc yields a 500 for that one request with no state corruption and no cross-request effect -- an availability nuisance the rules exclude.

findings.title: Entire /admin route group is registered without the auth middleware
findings.evidence: public/index.php:47-55 mounts the /tickets group and chains `->add(new AuthMiddleware($pdo));` at line 55. public/index.php:58-63 mounts the /admin group with tenants/sessions/logs/impersonate and closes at line 63 with no `->add(...)` of any kind. Slim only runs middleware that is attached, so every /admin route is served to an anonymous caller. AdminController::impersonate (AdminController.php:56-74) then mints a live 30-minute session for an arbitrary `user_id` and returns the bearer secret in the response body at line 73.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated caller reaches POST /admin/impersonate, supplies any user_id, and receives a working bearer token bound to that user's tenant_id -- full account and tenant takeover. GET /admin/sessions and /admin/tenants leak every live session prefix, user email and tenant billing email before that.
findings.recommendation: Attach an authenticating + role-checking middleware to the /admin group exactly as the /tickets group does, and gate impersonate on an operator role rather than on network placement.

triage.reason: Not a missing-header hygiene item: authentication is entirely absent on a route that mints credentials.

The comment at index.php:57 claims the console is 'only published on the internal VLAN', but nothing in this tree binds, filters or enforces that; the routes are on the same Slim app and the same listener as /tickets.
index.php:55 and index.php:63 re-read; the ->add() call is present on one group and absent on the other.
Ingress is the HTTP request itself; body parsed at AdminController.php:58, user_id read at :59.

scope.established_by: public/index.php:58-63 -- the /admin group closes without ->add(new AuthMiddleware($pdo))

searched.for: any middleware attached to the /admin group, or a global $app->add() that would cover it
searched.found: only the CORS closure at :25 and addErrorMiddleware at :39 are global; AuthMiddleware is attached to /tickets alone at :55

searched.for: an in-controller role or token check compensating for the missing middleware
searched.found: nothing -- no getAttribute('role'), no token read anywhere in the file

searched.for: an ip allowlist or admin gate that would narrow the exposure
searched.found: nothing

findings.title: status filter is concatenated into the SQL IN() list unescaped
findings.evidence: Sanitize.php:42-47 splits the caller's CSV and returns " AND status IN ('" . implode("','", $parts) . "')" with no quoting, escaping or allowlist. TicketController.php:35 appends that fragment straight onto the query string, and TicketController.php:40 hands the result to Db::all as raw SQL with only the tenant bound. Every sibling helper in the same class is safe by allowlist (sortColumn:28, direction:33) which is what makes this one look reviewed.
findings.impact: An authenticated requester sends ?status=x') OR 1=1 -- and drops the tenant predicate, reading every tenant's tickets; a UNION payload reaches the users and api_sessions tables in the same database.
findings.recommendation: Bind the status values as placeholders (build '?,?,?' from count($parts)) or intersect $parts against a fixed status allowlist the way sortColumn already does.

triage.reason: This is not paranoia about a safe library -- the fragment bypasses the prepared-statement layer it is concatenated into.
There is no mitigation to credit: array_filter/trim remove neither quotes nor comment markers.
Sanitize.php:47 and TicketController.php:35 re-read verbatim.
Ingress: TicketController.php:26 $request->getQueryParams(), field 'status', read at :35.

scope.established_by: Sanitize.php:47 builds a quoted SQL literal list by string concatenation
scope.narrowed_by: Reachable only behind AuthMiddleware (public/index.php:55), so the attacker needs any valid low-privilege token

searched.for: a second call site, or a caller that pre-validates the CSV
searched.found: exactly one call site, TicketController.php:35, with no validation before it

searched.for: escaping or quoting inside the query helper that would neutralise the fragment
searched.found: nothing -- Db::all:37 prepares whatever string it is given; PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES=false (Db.php:27) does not help a literal already in the SQL text

searched.for: a status allowlist analogous to 'sortable'
searched.found: nothing -- 'sortable' and 'fillable' exist, no status list

findings.title: Attachment download builds the path from the raw URL segment while its sibling handlers sanitise
findings.evidence: AttachmentController.php:53 does $path = $base . '/' . rawurldecode((string) $args['name']); -- no Sanitize::filename, unlike upload (:41) and remove (:71) which both call it. The route is declared with the greedy placeholder {name:.+} at public/index.php:53, so path separators survive routing, and rawurldecode additionally turns %2e%2e%2f into ../ after Slim has finished with it. Line 59 then file_get_contents($path) into the response body.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user reads any file the PHP process can open: GET /tickets/1/attachments/../../../../etc/passwd, or ../../config/settings.php and the .env it falls back to, which yields DB_DSN/DB_USER/DB_PASS.
findings.recommendation: Run the segment through Sanitize::filename like remove() does, then realpath() the result and reject anything that does not start with the ticket's attachment directory.

triage.reason: There is no mitigation on this path at all; the mitigation exists on the two sibling methods, which is the evidence that its absence here is the defect.
Lines 41, 53 and 71 re-read; the asymmetry is literal.
Ingress: the {name:.+} route argument declared at public/index.php:53, consumed at AttachmentController.php:53.

scope.established_by: AttachmentController.php:53 concatenates rawurldecode($args['name']) without Sanitize::filename
scope.narrowed_by: Requires a valid session token (public/index.php:55); read-only -- the write paths (upload/remove) are sanitised

searched.for: whether filename() would have blocked this input
searched.found: yes -- basename() plus a [^A-Za-z0-9._-] scrub at :18-19 removes separators; download simply never calls it

searched.for: a route constraint that would forbid slashes in {name}
searched.found: the opposite -- line 53 uses {name:.+} while the DELETE route at :54 uses the plain {name}

searched.for: a realpath/str_starts_with containment check after the concatenation
searched.found: nothing -- only is_file() at :55

findings.title: Ticket read and attachment handlers accept any ticket id with no tenant ownership check
findings.evidence: TicketController::show queries 'FROM tickets WHERE id = ?' with [$id] only (:52-53) and never reads the tenant_id attribute that AuthMiddleware set at AuthMiddleware.php:64 -- while TicketController::update, twenty lines below, does exactly that: 'WHERE id = ? AND tenant_id = ?' with [$id, $tenant] (:106-107). AttachmentController::upload/download/remove derive their directory from (int) $args['id'] alone (:24, :52, :70) and never consult tenant_id either.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user of any tenant enumerates ticket ids and reads other tenants' ticket bodies, comments and requester/assignee ids, and reads, overwrites or deletes attachments belonging to other tenants. Multi-tenant isolation is the security property this service exists to provide.
findings.recommendation: Add the tenant predicate to show() as update() already has it, and resolve the ticket (with its tenant) before touching the attachment directory in all three attachment handlers.

triage.reason: No hypothetical caller involved: the handler is the caller, and it is routed at public/index.php:50-54.
AuthMiddleware is an authentication control, not an authorization one -- it sets attributes and never compares them; there is no working mitigation being stretched.
TicketController.php:52 and :106 re-read; the two queries differ exactly as described.
Ingress: the {id} route argument (public/index.php:50), read at TicketController.php:47.

scope.established_by: TicketController.php:51-54 -- the lookup is keyed on the caller-supplied id alone
scope.narrowed_by: Requires any valid session token; TicketController::index (:34) and ::update (:106) are correctly scoped, so the gap is per-handler, not service-wide

searched.for: an authorization decision that would cover the handlers
searched.found: nothing -- :62-66 only attaches user_id/tenant_id/role attributes and calls the handler

searched.for: every place the tenant attribute is actually compared
searched.found: only TicketController.php:34 (index) and :106 (update); show and all of AttachmentController never reference it

findings.title: PATCH /tickets/{id} writes every body key to the row; the declared fillable allowlist is never read
findings.evidence: TicketController.php:113 takes the whole parsed body as $changes, :114 unsets only 'id' and 'created_at', and :122 passes the remainder straight to Db::update, which turns every key into a `col` = ? assignment (Db.php:67-70). config/settings.php:32 declares 'fillable' => ['subject','body','priority'] with the comment 'Fields a requester is allowed to change on a ticket they opened' -- and a repo-wide grep for 'fillable' returns that declaration and nothing else.
findings.impact: A requester PATCHes {"tenant_id": 7} and moves his own ticket into another tenant, or sets assignee_id/requester_id/status arbitrarily. Combined with the missing tenant check on show(), tenant_id rewriting is a two-step cross-tenant data path. Calibrated down from high at the critic stage: the write is confined to a ticket the caller already owns, so it injects and tampers rather than exfiltrating; cross-tenant reading is covered by the CWE-639 finding instead.
findings.recommendation: Intersect $changes with $this->settings['tickets']['fillable'] before calling Db::update -- the allowlist already exists and is already loaded into $this->settings.

triage.reason: Not defense-in-depth: the allowlist is the stated control and it is simply not wired up.
Db::update's table allowlist (Db.php:58) and backtick scrubbing (:68) are real and do work -- they stop table and identifier injection, but neither restricts which columns a requester may set.
settings.php:32 and TicketController.php:113-122 re-read; grep confirms zero consumers of 'fillable'.
Ingress: $request->getParsedBody() at TicketController.php:113 (body parsing enabled at public/index.php:19).

scope.established_by: TicketController.php:113-114 -- an unset() denylist of two keys stands in for the declared allowlist
scope.narrowed_by: Db.php:58 confines the write to the tickets table, and :114 protects id and created_at

searched.for: any consumer of the declared allowlist
searched.found: nothing -- config/settings.php:32 is the only occurrence in the tree

searched.for: a column allowlist inside the generic writer that would make the controller's omission harmless
searched.found: nothing -- WRITABLE (:17) allowlists tables only; columns come straight from the caller's array keys

findings.title: CORS reflects the caller's Origin and sets Allow-Credentials: true
findings.evidence: config/settings.php:24-25 sets allow_origin '*' and allow_credentials true. public/index.php:30 turns the wildcard into a reflection -- $allow = ($configured === '*' && $origin !== '') ? $origin : $configured; -- and :33-34 emit Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <caller's origin> together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Line 45 answers every preflight with 200. Reflected-origin plus credentials is precisely the combination the wildcard rule exists to forbid, and the reflection is what makes it legal to the browser.
findings.impact: Any web page a signed-in agent visits can issue credentialed cross-origin requests carrying the desk_session cookie that AuthMiddleware accepts (AuthMiddleware.php:37) and read the responses: full ticket read and PATCH-based write from an attacker's page, no token theft required.
findings.recommendation: Replace the reflection with a configured allowlist of partner origins, or keep the wildcard and set allow_credentials false and stop honouring the cookie fallback.

triage.reason: This is not a missing hardening header; it is an added header that grants an origin it should not.
The exploit needs no misuse by another component -- a browser executes it against the deployed config as written.
index.php:28-36 and settings.php:21-28 re-read verbatim.
Ingress: the Origin request header, read at public/index.php:29.

scope.established_by: public/index.php:30 substitutes the caller's Origin for the configured '*'
scope.narrowed_by: An operator who sets a concrete origin in settings.php:24 disables the reflection branch; the shipped default does not

searched.for: whether ambient cookie credentials are actually accepted (without that, the CORS reflection would be far less useful)
searched.found: they are -- :37 falls back to the desk_session cookie when no Authorization header is present

searched.for: a CSRF token check or SameSite enforcement anywhere in the stack
searched.found: nothing; the OPTIONS catch-all at :45 answers every preflight affirmatively

findings.title: Legacy search concatenates the q parameter into a raw query executed with PDO::query
findings.evidence: LegacySearchController.php:24 reads $q from the query string and :26-28 interpolate it twice into LIKE '%" . $q . "%' with no binding; :30 runs it through $this->pdo->query(), which does not parameterise at all. The defect is complete and self-contained inside this method.
findings.impact: If this controller is ever routed -- the class docstring says it is kept 'until the old console is finally decommissioned' -- it is an unauthenticated full-table-read SQL injection. In the tree as it stands nothing constructs it, so today it is dormant code carrying a live defect.
findings.recommendation: Delete the class, or bind $q as a parameter before anyone re-mounts it.

triage.reason: I traced reachability rather than dismissing it for being legacy: a repo-wide grep for LegacySearch returns only the class declaration itself, so it is not routed in public/index.php today. That is what caps the severity at low, not the file's name.
Rule 08 explicitly keeps a direct injection path in a function's own logic VALID even when nothing calls it, which is why this is reported rather than dropped.
File and lines 24-30 re-read verbatim.
No live ingress exists in this tree because the class is unrouted; the sink is intrinsic, which is the basis for reporting it under FP-08.

scope.established_by: LegacySearchController.php:26-28 -- string interpolation into the SQL text
scope.narrowed_by: Unrouted: public/index.php never imports or instantiates the class, so there is no path to it in the current tree

searched.for: a route, container binding or factory that would mount it
searched.found: only src/Controllers/LegacySearchController.php:16, the class declaration

searched.for: a PSR-4 autoload or script that would pull it into a running process on its own
searched.found: App\ => src/ autoload only, which makes it loadable but not reachable

findings.title: Session token digest compared with the loose != operator
findings.evidence: AuthMiddleware.php:58 reads if ($session['token_digest'] != $digest) -- loose, not strict, and not constant time. Both operands are 64-char sha256 hex from :43 and the api_sessions row.
findings.impact: Under PHP 8 two numeric strings still compare numerically, so two all-digit digests that differ only in leading zeros would compare equal; the probability of an all-digit sha256 hex digest is about 6e-14, so this is a correctness and side-channel defect rather than a practical bypass. The byte-wise early exit is also not constant time.
findings.recommendation: Use hash_equals($session['token_digest'], $digest).

triage.reason: I could not construct a triggerable path: forging a token whose digest is all-digits requires ~10^13 offline attempts per target row and gains nothing an attacker could not get by other means. Reported at low precisely because reproducibility is doubtful.
Comparing an authentication secret with != rather than hash_equals is a named weakness, not a style preference.
Line 58 re-read verbatim.
Ingress: the Authorization header or desk_session cookie at AuthMiddleware.php:34-37.

scope.established_by: AuthMiddleware.php:58 uses != on a secret digest
scope.narrowed_by: The prefix lookup at :50 narrows the comparison to a single row, and both operands are hex digests, which makes the numeric-juggling branch astronomically unlikely

searched.for: a second, strict comparison elsewhere on the path that would make this one redundant
searched.found: nothing -- :58 is the only place the full secret is verified

findings.title: SecureBox seals every value with a fixed all-zero IV in CBC mode
findings.evidence: crypto.dart:26 is static final enc.IV _iv = enc.IV.fromLength(16); -- sixteen zero bytes, shared by seal (:28-31) and open (:33-36), both AES-CBC. The comment at :24-25 explains the choice: a value sealed by one build must open in the next.
